chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Hasan ibn Kathir, from his father, who said:

An eye of a man was hit, and it was firm (in its place). So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ordered for his healthy eye to be tied up, and had a man stand beside him with an egg in his hand. He (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Can you see it?' So when he said 'Yes', he (peace be upon him) made him stand back a little, until it was hidden from him, he (peace be upon him) noted that place.

And the struck eye was tied up, and he made the man move further away while he was looking with his healthy eye, until it was hidden from him. Then he measured the distance between them, and he was given the 'arsh (compensation) for that.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (AS) determine compensation for partial blindness?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the early application of empirical observation in Islamic jurisprudence, where Imam Ali (AS) utilized a comparative visual acuity test to quantify injury for 'arsh (compensation). By establishing a measurable standard based on the distance at which an object becomes invisible to both the healthy and injured eyes, the Imam demonstrated a sophisticated understanding of ophthalmology and legal evidence. This method underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on rational deduction ('aql) and practical justice in determining financial liabilities for bodily harm.
